items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 3 at 3:42AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
A strong front moved toward the Kuskokwim Delta coast overnight.
Southerly onshore winds gusting up to 40 mph coupled with a
lengthy fetch will promote elevated water levels 1 to 2 feet above
normal high tide through early this morning morning. Strongest
winds are expected to peak this morning, with up to 0.5 inches of
rainfall. Areas of the coastline that are perpendicular to the
southerly wind direction, such as Kwigillingok, have a higher
chance of seeing impacts with this front. Strong south
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 2 at 9:09PM AKDT until September 5 at 11:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels 2.0 to 4.0 feet above the normal high tide
line.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast and Eastern Norton
Sound Coast from Golovin to Stebbins.

* WHEN...From 10 PM Thursday to 11 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels are expected to peak early
Friday morning during the time of high tide. While water
levels will subside somewhat later Friday, a second rise is
expected during the Saturday morning high tide
items.areas: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 2:13PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...A warm front associated with strong Bering Sea low will
move in Wednesday evening, with moderate to heavy rain and
gusty winds expected through Thursday. Rainfall totals are
expected to be around 1 to 1.50 inches, with wind gusts up to 55
mph out of the east/southeast.

* WHERE...St. Lawrence Island.

* WHEN...Wednesday September 2 through Thursday September 3.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain and gusty winds could make travel difficult
at times.
